title: google-deepmind/mujoco_playground
summary: MuJoCo Playground is an open-source library for GPU-accelerated robot learning, aimed at training control policies efficiently in simulation and carrying them over to real robots. It is useful as infrastructure for sim-to-real experiments, giving researchers a ready environment built around MuJoCo for scaling robot learning workflows rather than assembling the simulation and transfer stack from scratch.

extra.full_text: An open-source library for GPU-accelerated robot learning and sim-to-real transfer.

summary: DravenALG/awesome-vla-wam is a curated bibliography and resource list for Vision-Language-Action models and World Action Models, collecting research that connects perception, language, planning, and robot action. It is useful as a map of the fast-moving VLA/WAM literature rather than a runnable tool, helping researchers quickly find relevant papers, benchmarks, and related work around embodied AI and robot control.

title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python framework for writing GPU-accelerated simulation and computation code, aimed at robotics, machine learning, and physics-heavy workloads. It is useful when you want Python-level ergonomics while still targeting high-performance kernels for differentiable simulation, control, and other numerically intensive robot-AI pipelines.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack is a lightweight sim-to-real stack for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action models and RL agents without depending on ROS. It provides native MuJoCo/Gymnasium environments with synchronous execution across common robot platforms including Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101, and YAM, making it useful for researchers who want a leaner control and evaluation loop from simulation to hardware.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, SO101 and YAM.

title: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab
summary: ROBOTIS-GIT/cyclo_lab is a tutorial-oriented codebase for training robot policies with reinforcement learning and imitation learning on ROBOTIS platforms. It is aimed at bridging simulation and hardware by supporting Sim2Real deployment, so researchers can prototype learned behaviors in simulation and then run the resulting policies on real ROBOTIS robots.

extra.full_text: This repository provides tutorials for reinforcement learning and imitation learning using ROBOTIS robots, and supports Sim2Real functionality for deploying the learned policies on real robots.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable setup for building robotics simulation environments from interchangeable robot embodiments, objects, and scene components. It is aimed at rapidly prototyping simulated tasks and evaluating robot learning policies across diverse environment configurations, making it useful for scaling experiments without rebuilding each benchmark from scratch.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: Farama-Foundation/Metaworld
summary: MetaWorld is a suite of simulated robotic manipulation environments used to benchmark multi-task and meta-reinforcement-learning algorithms. It gives researchers a standardized set of robot tasks for testing whether agents can learn across tasks and adapt efficiently, making it useful for comparing generalization and transfer in robot learning.

extra.full_text: Collections of robotics environments geared towards benchmarking multi-task and meta reinforcement learning

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv implementation for training basic quadruped locomotion policies across multiple robot platforms. It is aimed at practical locomotion experimentation, including sim-to-sim transfer and sim-to-real deployment pipelines, so it should be useful as a starting point for researchers moving learned gaits from IsaacLab into other simulators or hardware.

extra.full_text: An IsaacLab DirectEnv for basic quadrupedal locomotion tasks, with support for multiple quadruped robots, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real pipelines

title: flexivrobotics/isaac_sim_ws
summary: flexivrobotics/isaac_sim_ws brings Flexiv robots into NVIDIA Isaac Sim with control paths that mirror the real hardware stack. It lets users drive simulated robots through Flexiv Elements Studio or the Flexiv RDK while using the same force/torque controller deployed on physical Flexiv robots, making it useful for testing control workflows in simulation before moving to the lab.

extra.full_text: Add Flexiv robots to Isaac Sim and control them using Flexiv Elements Studio or Flexiv RDK with the actual force/torque controller used on real robots.

title: RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse
summary: RoboVerse aims to bundle a unified platform, dataset, and benchmark for robot learning, with an emphasis on making training and evaluation scale across tasks and embodiments. The repo is positioned as infrastructure for testing whether robot policies generalize, rather than just demonstrating performance in isolated environments.

extra.full_text: RoboVerse: Towards a Unified Platform, Dataset and Benchmark for Scalable and Generalizable Robot Learning

title: dartsim/dart
summary: DART is a research-oriented C++23 physics engine for robotics, animation, and machine-learning workflows, with Python bindings for easier experimentation. It is useful when researchers need a programmable dynamics simulator rather than a black-box environment, especially for work involving robot modeling, contact dynamics, control, and simulation-driven learning.

title: D-Robotics/hobot_stereonet
summary: Hobot StereoNet uses a deep stereo matching model to turn paired camera images into real-time depth maps for robotics and computer vision systems. It is aimed at practical 3D perception, where fast, accurate depth from standard stereo inputs can support navigation, obstacle avoidance, and scene understanding.

title: NuclearVenom/BulletLab
summary: BulletLab turns PyBullet URDF robots into Python objects with a higher-level interface, so experiments can be built around robot parts, controls, telemetry, and visualization instead of low-level simulator plumbing. It pairs that object model with an ImGui-based UI and reinforcement-learning workflow support, making it useful for quickly inspecting, controlling, and instrumenting simulated robots during robotics experiments.

extra.full_text: A robotics experimentation framework build over PyBullet that transforms URDF models into intuitive Python objects, with modern ImGui-based UI, controls, telemetry, visualization, and reinforcement learning workflows.
